title: The 4:10
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Monday. The 4:10 from Eugene. The strip goes to the bus stop. Wood doesn't. She's on it. Two bags. The strip draws her getting off; nobody's there to meet her; the strip is. She looks at where the strip would be standing and shakes her head.

panels.composition: The Greyhound stop on 101, June, dry for once. The 4:10 pulling in. No one on the bench.

image.prompt: an intercity bus pulling into a roadside stop on a coastal highway on a dry June afternoon, an empty bench under a small shelter, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The door folding open. CHLOE stepping down with two bags. The Discman. The cardigan, in June. Hair longer.

image.prompt: a young woman with smudged eyeliner and a Discman on her belt stepping off a bus with two bags, wearing an oversized cardigan in summer, black and white, no words
image.notes: Chloe home for the summer. The strip is here; Wood isn't.

panels.composition: Chloe on the gravel. Looking at the empty bench. At the spot beside it where someone would stand. Nobody.

image.prompt: a young woman standing on gravel beside an empty bus-stop bench looking at the empty space next to it, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Chloe walking toward town with the bags, small. The bus pulling away. The strip drew this. Wood was at the shack. The strip tells him later.

image.prompt: a young woman walking toward a small town along a highway shoulder with two bags as a bus pulls away behind her, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: She's on it. The strip goes; Wood doesn't. The crab in the margin.
